newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe names go-between in Cr Foncier saga.
newsitem.headline: Juppe names go-between in Cr Foncier saga.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday he had named a go-between in the dispute at troubled home loans group Credit Foncier de France, as a four-day staff siege of the group's Paris headquarters dragged into its fourth day.

Juppe named Philippe Rouvillois, former SNCF state railways boss, as go-between in a dispute where employees and unions are fighting a government plan to break up Credit Foncier, spin part of it off to cooperative home loans group Credit Immobilier and wind the rest down.
Credit Foncier chairman Jerome Meyssonnier, who is being held at the Paris headquarters, declared himself a hostage on Monday and said he had broken off negotiations with the unions.
Juppe also called on staff at the group's headquarters to "re-establish normal working conditions as soon as possible".

More than 1,000 staff continued the siege on Monday after several hundred spent the weekend, many accompanied by their children, at the Paris premises where the peaceful siege began around midday on Friday.

"He's not our hostage, he's the finance ministry's hostage," one union official told Reuters at the scene, referring to Meyssonnier's difficult task of trying to find a solution to the crisis under pressure from the finance ministry.
"The ball is in their court now," she added.

Another union official at the premises said national union leaders Marc Blondel, of the Workers' Force (Force Ouvriere) union, and Marc Viannet of the Communist-led CGT union were expected to turn up later in a show of support.
Unions decided on Monday to continue the dispute but made sure Credit Foncier branches opened for business as usual as they battle for public sympathy under hefty media coverage of their dispute.
Employees from the French central bank were also expected to turn up to show support later in the day, one staff union representative said.
